risks: WP-39 and WP-44 name identical contracts/commands/repository paths. Independent creation would overwrite accepted foundation work; one files-domain owner must integrate extensions.

WP-44 migration names comment_anchor/document_revision also owned conceptually by WP-15; a second schema/comment store would violate one authority. Ownership and actual migrator filename require accepted receipts.

Existing filesystem allowlists are useful standalone safety, not proof of resource ACL. Legacy path/native/tool readers and writes can bypass shared authority unless the single-writer guard covers them.

Current image storage resizes original bytes before write; preserving only originalSize is not provenance or immutable binary preservation. Coordinate repair through WP-39 rather than layering another store.
PDF embedded annotation layer and CodePreviewOverlay write badge are misleading near-matches to domain requirements; neither proves annotation persistence or revisioned editing.

Shared video seek is currently absent in classifier/dispatcher. Decoder readiness, browser codecs, duration/units, range-capable authorized delivery and unsupported-format fallback need concrete acceptance, not a fake player.
Annotation anchor strings have no PDF/media encoding specified; schemaVersion minimum 0 conflicts with positive persisted schema_version unless accepted validation/migration semantics are explicit.

Public bundle copies raw HTML and optional raw snapshot. Manifest allowlisting cannot protect private annotations embedded in those bytes or retroactively revoke a downloaded public copy; public and authenticated sharing must be distinguished.

Preview/parser XSS, SVG/HTML active content, hostile PDFs, decompression/size limits, binary conversion failures and sandbox/license assumptions must be exercised, not inferred from pdf.js worker usage.
Path-only preview caches/async loads can retain old revision or expose newly revoked metadata. Guard future fetch/delivery/display; do not promise already-read bytes become unread.
Five headline scenarios do not waive full search/mentions/notifications/activity/agent/observability/offline DoD. Missing foundation integrations are separately recorded, not N/A.

Root-owned wave0 changes can stale these inspected source bytes; validator failure identifies invalidated references and requires targeted reread before acceptance. No runtime completeness claim is made.
